channel.title: Word of the Day
channel.description: One word, what it means, and where it came from. A Day News demo feed.

item.title: halcyon
item.description:
halcyon · adjective

Calm and peaceful; happy and carefree, especially when remembered from the past.

“They looked back on the halcyon days of their first summer by the lake.”

The word comes from the Greek alkyōn, a kingfisher. In ancient legend the bird nested on the sea around the winter solstice and calmed the waves while it did.

item.title: petrichor
item.description:
petrichor · noun

The pleasant, earthy smell that rises when rain falls on dry ground.

“After the storm, the whole garden smelled of petrichor.”

Coined in 1964 by the Australian scientists Isabel Joy Bear and Richard Thomas, from the Greek petra, “stone,” and ichor, the fluid said to flow in the veins of the gods.

item.title: serendipity
item.description:
serendipity · noun

The luck of finding something good or useful without looking for it.

“By pure serendipity, the bookshop they ducked into out of the rain had the atlas they wanted.”

Coined by the English writer Horace Walpole in 1754, after a Persian fairy tale, The Three Princes of Serendip, whose heroes kept making discoveries by accident.

item.title: gossamer
item.description:
gossamer · noun, adjective

Fine, filmy cobwebs that drift through the air in calm weather; anything very light, thin and delicate.

“Morning light caught the gossamer strung between the fence posts.”

Probably from Middle English gossomer, “goose summer,” the mild weather late in the year when such webs are often seen.

item.title: lunation
item.description:
lunation · noun

The time from one new moon to the next, about 29.5 days; a lunar month.

“The village market is held once every lunation.”

From Medieval Latin lunatio, from Latin luna, “moon.”

item.title: meander
item.description:
meander · verb

To follow a winding course; to wander without hurry or aim.

“The path meanders through the meadow down to the river.”

From the Maeander, the ancient name of a river in western Turkey, now the Büyük Menderes, famous for its looping bends.
